years.title: The 2026 budget
years.simple: This is the government's plan for spending in 2026, the biggest in Nigeria's history. It expects to collect ₦36.87 trillion, so almost half of the plan (₦31.46 trillion) is a gap, to be filled mostly by borrowing. In the first half of 2026, debts were paid in full, but ministries got nothing for 2026 projects. They were still spending the 2025 projects budget.
years.splitHeadline: Almost half is planned for projects, and nearly a quarter for paying debts
years.splitSub: Federal budget as signed into law. Figures from the Budget Office.
years.splitNote: "Projects" here includes projects paid for by loans, aid and government-owned companies, not only ministries. Ministries' own projects are ₦15.68 trillion of it.

verdict.text: Ministries got ₦0 for 2026 projects by 30 June 2026
Debts were paid in full: ₦7.90 trillion. For every ₦100 the government collected, ₦66 went on debts
The government collected ₦11.88 trillion, about two-thirds of what it planned for January to June
For every ₦100 it spent, about ₦42 was borrowed, mostly from lenders inside Nigeria

years.title: The 2025 budget
years.totalNote: Signed at ₦54.99 trillion in February 2025, then cut to ₦48.32 trillion in December 2025.
years.simple: This was the government's plan for spending in 2025. It was signed at ₦54.99 trillion. In December 2025, after little money had been released for projects, it was cut to ₦48.32 trillion, mostly by reducing projects. The projects part was extended four times and is still being spent in 2026.
years.splitHeadline: After the cut, about a third was for projects and nearly a third for paying debts
years.splitSub: The 2025 budget as re-enacted in December 2025. Figures from the Budget Office.
years.splitNote: Before the cut, ₦23.44 trillion of the ₦54.99 trillion was for projects (Budget Office report for April to June 2025).

verdict.text: By September 2025, less than ₦0.5 trillion had been released to ministries for 2025 projects
Debts got more than planned: ₦12.63 trillion. For every ₦100 the government collected, ₦68 went on debts
The government collected ₦18.63 trillion, about 6 in 10 naira of what it planned
The budget was cut from ₦54.99 trillion to ₦48.32 trillion in December 2025, mostly from projects

progress.headline: Debts got more than planned, while ministries got about 1 in 10 naira planned for projects
progress.title: Plan versus what happened (January to September 2025)
progress.note: "Planned" is three-quarters of the yearly budget as cut in December 2025. From the Budget Office's reviewed report for July to September 2025, published 24 August 2026.

rows.label: All project spending
rows.more: This includes projects paid for by loans, aid and government-owned companies.

rows.label: Released to ministries for 2025 projects
rows.more: ₦34.32 billion (January to March), ₦393.86 billion (April to June) and ₦16.08 billion (July to September).

gaps: The Budget Office reports disagree with each other on project money released to ministries. The text of each report adds up to about ₦444 billion by September 2025. A table in the July to September report shows only ₦17.71 billion. We show the larger figure.

The President's December 2025 budget speech said ₦3.10 trillion had been released for 2025 projects by September 2025. That is far more than the Budget Office reports show for ministries. The two may count different things.
We have not found a final report for the whole of 2025.
The reports do not list which projects the money paid for.
